name: Bolivia
headline: Bolivia: −1.6% growth in 2025, 19.5% inflation, debt 83% of GDP
sections: Bolivia is a $65.2 billion economy (2025), the world's 92nd-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew −1.6% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $13K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 13.1% of GDP (2024).

Consumer prices rose 19.5% in 2025, well above typical central bank targets, up from 1.7% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 3.3% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 5.0% (2025).
Gross government debt is 83% of GDP (2025), a elevated level that has risen from 68% in 2020. The general government balance is −11.4% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is −1.9% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 47% of GDP (2024), a relatively closed economy. Net FDI inflows were 0.8% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 82% of GDP by 2031, broadly stable from today's level. Life expectancy is 68.7 years (2024). Population: 12.6 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
